features.name: Development Tool Shell
features.purpose: Provides the single persistent status bar and primary navigation that frames every screen, replacing the prior marketing-style header and footer with a compact, information-dense developer-tool bar.

invocation.trigger: Any screen loads, or the working directory, round, or default provider/model changes.

inputs.name: working_directory_path
inputs.description: The path of the currently open project.

inputs.name: current_round_number
inputs.description: The round currently active in the project.

inputs.name: default_provider_and_model
inputs.description: The provider and model configured as the project default.

inputs.name: app_version
inputs.description: The running version of the tool.

inputs.name: viewport_width
inputs.description: Available horizontal space, used to decide what truncates.

outputs.primary: A rendered status bar and four-item navigation.
outputs.format: Persistent header row plus navigation row on every screen.
outputs.schema_notes: Slots for path, round, provider/model, version, and links to Project, Artifacts, Settings, and Docs.

success_criteria: Round, provider+model, and version are always fully visible regardless of width
Only the working-directory path ever truncates, always from its start, leaving the project name visible
No external-link drawer, footer, or landing page appears anywhere
A single accent color marks every primary action, active nav state, and focus indicator
Vertical spacing is visibly tighter than the prior register

failure_modes.mode: Wrong element truncates under extreme narrowness
failure_modes.mitigation: Enforce a fixed truncation order with the directory path always first

failure_modes.mode: Two accent colors compete for primary emphasis
failure_modes.mitigation: Restrict the accent color to a single role across the app

features.name: Open To The Project
features.purpose: Sends the user straight into their current project when one is already known, removing any need for an introductory screen.

invocation.trigger: The app is opened at its root address.

inputs.name: remembered_working_directory
inputs.description: A previously opened project directory, if one is remembered.

outputs.primary: Either the project view or the directory picker.
outputs.format: Full-screen navigation to exactly one destination.
outputs.schema_notes: Never shows both destinations at once.

success_criteria: With a remembered directory, the project view appears with no intermediate screen
With no remembered directory, the directory picker appears immediately
No introduction or landing screen is ever shown

failure_modes.mode: A remembered directory no longer exists
failure_modes.mitigation: Fall back to the directory picker and let the user choose again

failure_modes.mode: Stale directory memory opens the wrong project
failure_modes.mitigation: Always show the working-directory path prominently so the user can confirm

features.name: Round Tree
features.purpose: Shows the current round's full set of planning artifacts as a single ordered list, so the user can see at a glance what exists, what's stale, and what's missing.

invocation.trigger: The project view is opened, or an artifact's underlying data changes.

inputs.name: current_round_artifacts
inputs.description: Every artifact expected in the current round.

inputs.name: artifact_dependency_graph
inputs.description: Which artifacts depend on which others, used to compute staleness.

outputs.primary: An ordered list of artifact lines with status and lane.
outputs.schema_notes: Each line carries artifact name, status (present, needs update, or missing), and lane (prompt, reference, or record).

success_criteria: Artifacts always appear in pipeline order
An artifact whose upstream source changed after it was produced shows as needing an update
The round's usage record never shows as needing an update
Each line's lane matches the three-item legend
Selecting a line opens that artifact's detail view

failure_modes.mode: Status miscalculated because an upstream timestamp is missing
failure_modes.mitigation: Treat unknown upstream state as needing an update rather than marking it present

failure_modes.mode: A lane is mis-colored
failure_modes.mitigation: Derive lane strictly from a fixed artifact-to-lane mapping

features.name: Agent Rows
features.purpose: Lists the seven planning agents in pipeline order as compact rows, each showing its produced artifact, the model it last used, this round's token counts, and the single next action available.

invocation.trigger: The project view is opened, or an agent's run state changes.

inputs.name: agent_pipeline_order
inputs.description: The fixed sequence of the seven agents.

inputs.name: per_agent_last_model
inputs.description: The model each agent last ran with this round, blank if not yet run.

inputs.name: per_agent_tokens_in_out
inputs.description: Tokens consumed and produced this round for each agent.

inputs.name: per_agent_run_state
inputs.description: The agent's current state used to decide which action to show.

outputs.primary: Seven compact rows, one per agent.
outputs.format: One row per agent, fixed pipeline order.
outputs.schema_notes: Each row has agent name, artifact name, last-run model, tokens in/out, and one action.

success_criteria: Rows appear in fixed pipeline order with no numbering
The shown action always matches the agent's real state
A model name only appears once that agent has actually run this round
Choosing the action routes to the correct next screen for that agent

failure_modes.mode: Shown action does not match actual state after a run completes
failure_modes.mitigation: Recompute state from the same usage record and dependency graph the round tree uses

failure_modes.mode: Token counts fail to update after a run
failure_modes.mitigation: Refresh counts from the same record the round cost reads

features.name: Round Cost
features.purpose: Gives an at-a-glance estimate of how much the current round has spent so far, based on recorded token usage.

invocation.trigger: The project view is opened, or the round's usage record changes.

inputs.name: round_usage_totals
inputs.description: Aggregated token and cost totals for the round.

outputs.primary: A labelled cost estimate with token counts.
outputs.schema_notes: Names any call excluded from the estimate because it could not be priced.

success_criteria: The figure is always labelled as an estimate
Token totals are shown alongside the cost
Any unpriced call is named rather than silently folded into the total
The estimate is never shown as a zero value when the true cost is unknown

failure_modes.mode: A provider's pricing is unavailable
failure_modes.mitigation: Exclude and name that call rather than assume zero cost

failure_modes.mode: Totals lag behind the latest run
failure_modes.mitigation: Recompute from the same usage record every time the view opens

features.name: Artifact View
features.purpose: Lets the user open and read any artifact from the current or a past round, with the file's content, status, and location shown together.

invocation.trigger: A round-tree line, an artifact link, or the Artifacts navigation item is chosen.

inputs.name: selected_round
inputs.description: The round whose artifacts should be listed.

inputs.name: selected_artifact_path
inputs.description: The specific artifact to display.

outputs.format: A round selector and artifact tree on one side, the file's content on the other.
outputs.schema_notes: Header line gives path, size, last-modified time, and lane; text content is line-numbered, structured content is pretty-printed; a missing file shows which agent would produce it instead of content.

success_criteria: Every round on disk appears in the round selector, defaulting to the active round
The tree beside the content uses the same lanes and status flags as the project view
The selected file is visibly marked in the tree
A missing artifact shows its producing agent's name instead of an error
Only files belonging to the reviewed artifact set can ever be opened this way
A download option is always available, and the design mock additionally offers a rendered preview in a new view

failure_modes.mode: A request targets a path outside the recognized artifact set
failure_modes.mitigation: Resolve only files in the fixed artifact table, under the project's own planning folder, and reject anything else

failure_modes.mode: A very large file slows the view
failure_modes.mitigation: Still render with line numbers without blocking navigation

failure_modes.mode: Round selector omits a round present on disk
failure_modes.mitigation: Rescan available rounds each time the view opens

features.name: Artifact Links
features.purpose: Makes every artifact reachable from wherever it's mentioned — navigation, round tree, and chat downloads — so the user is never more than one choice away from seeing a file.

invocation.trigger: The navigation is rendered, a round-tree line is rendered, or a download option is rendered in the chat frame.

inputs.name: artifact_identity
inputs.description: The artifact and round a given link should point to.

outputs.primary: A link that opens the artifact view at the right file.
outputs.format: An inline link beside or in place of existing entries.
outputs.schema_notes: One link per artifact reference, always pointing at the matching file and round.

success_criteria: The Artifacts destination sits between Project and Settings in the navigation
Every round-tree line opens the artifact view at that exact file
Every download option in the chat frame's action row is paired with an equivalent option that opens the file instead of downloading it

failure_modes.mode: A link opens the wrong round's version of a file
failure_modes.mitigation: Always carry the round identity together with the file identity

failure_modes.mode: A new download option is added without its matching open option
failure_modes.mitigation: Derive both options from one shared list of artifacts

features.name: Chat Frame Register
features.purpose: Keeps the conversation screen's full set of existing functions — agent progress, transcript, live indicators, retries, downloads — while presenting them in the plain, low-chrome developer-tool style.

invocation.trigger: A conversation with any agent is opened or continues.

inputs.name: agent_pipeline_state
inputs.description: Which agents are completed, active, or unreachable.

inputs.name: transcript_messages
inputs.description: The conversation history for the current agent.

inputs.name: live_run_progress
inputs.description: Character and elapsed-time counters for an in-progress run.

inputs.name: run_cost_summary
inputs.description: The cost of a completed run.

outputs.format: Plain-text agent progress row, block-style transcript, action row, and composer.
outputs.schema_notes: Exactly one primary action per row; a completed run's cost appears as the same summary style used for round cost.

success_criteria: Every function present before the rework still works: progress indicators, turn tokens, fast-forward with its explanation, retry, alternative-response choice, downloads, continue actions, composer, model indicator, status line

The agent progress row shows plain text only, active agent marked the same way as the active nav item, completed agents at full emphasis, unreachable agents dimmed with their explanation still available, no connecting marks between them
Duplicated back-navigation controls are gone, since the agent progress row and the status bar's project link already provide that path
Transcript messages read as plain blocks with a dimmed one-word label, no fill color, and a neutral marker on the user's own messages
A completed run's cost renders in the same three-line style as round cost
Exactly one primary-emphasis action appears per row, with all others neutral
The live-activity indicator is the only moving element on screen

failure_modes.mode: A function is silently dropped during the visual rework
failure_modes.mitigation: Verify each pre-existing function against a checklist before release

failure_modes.mode: Removed back-navigation leaves a dead end
failure_modes.mitigation: Confirm the agent progress row and status bar project link always remain reachable

features.name: Entry Screens Register
features.purpose: Brings the directory picker and the project-mode question in line with the developer-tool look while keeping their exact existing behavior.

invocation.trigger: The directory picker or the project-mode question is shown.

inputs.name: candidate_directories
inputs.description: Subdirectories available to browse into.

inputs.name: current_path_input
inputs.description: The path currently typed or selected.

outputs.primary: The reworked picker and question screens.
outputs.format: Single-column directory list, one-row folder-creation entry, two-line question with two side-by-side choices.
outputs.schema_notes: Exactly one primary-emphasis action on each screen.

success_criteria: Directory names and the path entry render in fixed-width type
Subdirectories list one per line rather than as a grid
The folder-creation option and its text entry share one row
The question's explanation is no longer than two lines and its two choices sit on one row, one of them primary
The picker still browses, creates, and selects a directory exactly as before
The question is still asked once per session

failure_modes.mode: A long directory name breaks the single-column layout
failure_modes.mitigation: Truncate the name rather than wrap or overflow

failure_modes.mode: The reworked question is asked more than once per session
failure_modes.mitigation: Keep the existing once-per-session behavior unchanged

features.name: Setup Wizard Register
features.purpose: Presents the existing three-step setup in the same terse developer-tool style, dropping explanatory prose and alert-style notices while keeping every field and step working exactly as before.

invocation.trigger: Setup is opened for an unconfigured provider, or the user revisits an existing step.

inputs.name: provider_choice
inputs.description: The provider being configured.

inputs.name: key_entry
inputs.description: The credential entered for the provider.

inputs.name: model_choice
inputs.description: The default model selected for the provider.

outputs.format: A compact step indicator with one short title and one primary action per step.
outputs.schema_notes: The never-stored-outside-your-system notice becomes one dimmed line under the key entry; the connected-provider notice becomes one dimmed line above the model choice; the free-tier notice is removed.

success_criteria: Each step keeps its fields, identifiers, and validation exactly as before
Each step shows exactly one primary action (Connect, then Continue)
Clearing saved credentials is a neutral, warning-toned action
The within-wizard back action has no directional mark
No action in the wizard returns to the directory picker

failure_modes.mode: Removing prose accidentally removes needed guidance
failure_modes.mitigation: Keep the single dimmed line carrying the essential notice

failure_modes.mode: A step's validation regresses during the visual rework
failure_modes.mitigation: Keep field identifiers and validation logic untouched

features.name: Gate Card Register
features.purpose: Turns the shared per-agent model gate into a compact one-line panel naming the agent and its default model, with a small, clear set of choices, reused identically wherever a model must be confirmed.

invocation.trigger: An agent is about to run and its model has not yet been confirmed for this round.

inputs.name: agent_name
inputs.description: The agent the gate is confirming a model for.

inputs.name: default_model
inputs.description: The model that would be used if the default is accepted.

inputs.name: current_selection_state
inputs.description: Whether a model has already been chosen or kept for this agent.

outputs.format: One monospace naming line plus a two- or three-action row.
outputs.schema_notes: 'Use default' is primary; 'Pick a model' and 'Keep <model>' are neutral; picking expands the setup wizard's model fields inline.

success_criteria: The panel's first line names the agent and its default model in fixed-width type
Exactly one component serves all seven agents and the Designer entry point
Expanding 'Pick a model' reveals the same fields the setup wizard uses
The separate agent-name heading above the panel on the Designer entry point is gone, since the status bar and agent progress row already name the agent
The underlying selection identifiers, behavior, and capability check are unchanged

failure_modes.mode: The panel diverges from the setup wizard's fields over time
failure_modes.mitigation: Keep the expanded fields sourced from the same definition as the setup wizard

failure_modes.mode: Removing the heading leaves the Designer entry point unclear about which agent is active
failure_modes.mitigation: Confirm the status bar and agent progress row always name the current agent

features.name: Designer Wizard Register
features.purpose: Brings the seven-step Designer flow in line with the developer-tool look — trimming explanatory text and decorative step markers — while keeping every step, field, and outcome the same.

invocation.trigger: The Designer agent's gate is passed and its multi-step flow begins.

inputs.name: current_step_index
inputs.description: Which of the seven steps is active.

inputs.name: uploaded_reference_material
inputs.description: Screenshots or reference images supplied for the design.

inputs.name: generated_mock_state
inputs.description: Whether a mock has been generated, approved, or needs regeneration.

outputs.format: A plain-text step row plus one instruction line and one primary action per step.
outputs.schema_notes: Upload zones are a plain dashed outline with one dimmed line of text; approval and disclaimer notices are single dimmed lines, not alerts.

success_criteria: The step row renders as plain text with no circular markers or check marks; the active step is marked the same way as the active nav item, completed steps at full emphasis, later steps dimmed
Each step shows at most one instruction line and exactly one primary action
The introductory paragraph and usage explanation are gone
The look-and-feel disclaimer and the approval notice each render as a single dimmed line
The live preview, its full-view option, the cost summary, and the retry option all keep working exactly as before

failure_modes.mode: Removing the usage explanation leaves new users confused about a step's purpose
failure_modes.mitigation: Keep the one-line instruction on every step

failure_modes.mode: The step row becomes ambiguous about which step is active once icons are removed
failure_modes.mitigation: Reuse the exact active/complete/dimmed marking used in the agent progress row

features.name: Per-Agent Effort
features.purpose: Lets a reasoning-effort level be chosen per agent alongside its model, so agents that need deeper reasoning can use it while others stay fast and cheap.

invocation.trigger: A model is resolved for an agent, in the gate panel or the setup wizard's model step.

inputs.name: resolved_model_capabilities
inputs.description: The effort levels the chosen model actually supports.

inputs.name: chosen_effort
inputs.description: The effort level selected for the agent, or for the default.

outputs.primary: The stored effort choice for an agent, or for the default.
outputs.format: One value alongside the model in the same selection record.
outputs.schema_notes: Allowed values are always 'default' plus low, medium, high, with xhigh or max appearing only when the resolved model supports them.

success_criteria: The offered effort values always match what the resolved model actually supports
An agent left on 'default' inherits the default's effort exactly as it inherits its model
The effort appears after the model name wherever the model is shown, but only when it isn't 'default'
Every run records which effort was actually used
An unsupported effort value never causes a run to fail
The gate, the model indicator, the retry flow, and the setup wizard all read and write the same stored value

failure_modes.mode: A model's supported effort levels are misreported
failure_modes.mitigation: Trust only the resolved capability check, never an assumed list

failure_modes.mode: An unsupported effort value is sent to a model that rejects it
failure_modes.mitigation: Drop the parameter silently rather than let the run fail

failure_modes.mode: Gate and wizard fall out of sync on the stored value
failure_modes.mitigation: Keep one single read/write path for the field

nfr_goals: A single accent color and consistent low-chrome visual language across every screen, with no exceptions
Provider credentials remain visible only to the user's own browser and are never transmitted elsewhere or written to disk
The status bar's round, provider, model, and version stay fully legible regardless of window width
Cost and token figures stay accurate and reflect the latest completed run, never showing an unknown cost as zero
The visual register rework is complete after this round, with no screens left needing it
